items.title: CVE-2026-131914: Idunno Idunno AntiCsrf Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A deserialization vulnerability in Idunno AntiCsrf allows remote code execution, necessitating immediate removal or patching.
items.summary: The Idunno AntiCsrf library contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via object injection. CISA has added this to its KEV catalog, noting that the product may be end-of-life or end-of-service. Federal agencies are required to remediate or discontinue use by November 27, 2026.
items.bottom_line: If your stack includes the Idunno AntiCsrf library, you should transition to a supported alternative immediately as it is now a tracked KEV.

items.title: CVE-2026-103406: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router OS Command Injection Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Critical RCE vulnerability in HPE Juniper networking gear requires immediate patching or mitigation to prevent root-level compromise.
items.summary: HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Router devices are vulnerable to an OS command injection flaw that allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code as root. The vulnerability is triggered by a specially crafted salt minion ID. CISA has added this to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog and mandates federal remediation by November 28, 2026.
items.bottom_line: If you manage HPE Juniper Session Smart appliances, you must apply vendor mitigations or discontinue use immediately to comply with CISA's BOD 26-04 requirements.

items.title: CVE-2026-123633 Portfolio Status: Impact of NGINX Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Critical NGINX vulnerabilities in Palo Alto Networks products allow RCE; disable HTTP/2 if patching is not immediate.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has identified two critical NGINX vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007) affecting its PAN-OS and Panorama products when HTTP/2 is enabled. The flaws involve use-after-free and integer underflow issues that can lead to worker process crashes or arbitrary code execution. The company has released remediations and advises customers to disable HTTP/2 if they cannot patch immediately.
items.bottom_line: Administrators must verify their PAN-OS/Panorama configurations and either patch or disable HTTP/2 to mitigate potential RCE attacks.

items.title: EU Academy Users’ Names and Emails Exposed in EU Commission Hack
items.one_liner: A suspected China-backed cyberattack on the EU Commission has leaked user data and remains active within internal systems.
items.summary: The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack on the EU Academy platform that resulted in the theft of user names and email addresses. The attack, which began on October 22, is suspected to be the work of China-backed threat actors using an AI-powered penetration testing tool called ARTEX. While the Commission has taken internal applications offline as a precaution, the breach is reportedly still spreading through internal networks.

items.bottom_line: The ongoing breach of EU Commission systems via AI-driven tools highlights a significant escalation in sophisticated, persistent threats against government infrastructure.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco Unveil AI-Assisted Linux Security Tool to Block Exploits Before Patching
items.one_liner: A new eBPF-based runtime security tool that lets AI agents inject temporary, non-disruptive shields to block exploits before patches are ready.
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco have launched Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime security tool that uses AI agents to deploy eBPF-based shields. The tool allows defenders to block exploits in real-time without patching or system restarts by injecting targeted mitigations into the kernel. It is built on the foundation of the Tetragon security platform and is designed to protect infrastructure while security teams test and roll out permanent fixes.
items.bottom_line: You can now use AI-generated eBPF shields to protect vulnerable Linux systems from active exploits without requiring service downtime or immediate patching.

items.title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in network security expansion
items.one_liner: CrowdStrike is acquiring Zscaler for $43.9 billion to unite endpoint security and zero-trust network access for modern cloud architectures.
items.summary: CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion to merge endpoint protection with cloud network security. The acquisition combines CrowdStrike's device and cloud workload monitoring with Zscaler's zero-trust network access control, addressing security requirements as corporate systems and AI agents connect directly to cloud applications. CrowdStrike plans to integrate device telemetry with network connection logs and cross-sell both platforms to Zscaler's roughly 8,000 customers. Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry will continue leading the business and join CrowdStrike's board upon closing, which is expected in the second half of fiscal 2028 pending regulatory and shareholder approvals.

items.title: Hackers Exploited CVSS 10.0 Hex.pm RCE Flaw to Compromise 6 Package Registry Servers
items.one_liner: A decade-old RCE vulnerability in the Hex.pm package registry was exploited, necessitating a full security reset for all users.
items.summary: The Hex.pm package registry for Elixir and Erlang was compromised after attackers exploited a CVSS 10.0 remote code execution vulnerability. The flaw, which existed since 2016, allowed unauthenticated attackers to execute OS commands by sending a crafted request body containing an Elixir struct. While the registry was patched within 15 minutes of detection, users are advised to reset passwords and 2FA, as account data may have been exposed.
items.bottom_line: If you have a Hex.pm account, you must reset your password and 2FA immediately to mitigate the risk of credential exposure.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE
items.one_liner: A critical RCE in a 2008-era ASP.NET library is being actively exploited; remove it immediately as no patch is coming.
items.summary: A critical, unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability, CVE-2026-131914, has been discovered in the legacy ASP.NET library Idunno.AntiCsrf. The flaw allows attackers to execute arbitrary code via a single HTTP POST request by exploiting insecure deserialization in the library's AntiCsrfModule. Because the project has been defunct since 2008, no official patch will be released, and organizations are urged to remove the library immediately.
items.bottom_line: If your legacy ASP.NET applications use Idunno.AntiCsrf, you are vulnerable to unauthenticated RCE and must replace the library immediately.

items.title: ARTEX and Friends: Enter Agentic Offensive Frameworks
items.one_liner: Threat actors are actively deploying agentic LLM pentesting frameworks like ARTEX and CAIRN to automate multi-stage intrusions at machine speed.
items.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant have observed multiple threat actors weaponizing open-source agentic pentesting frameworks—such as ARTEX, Hexstrike, CAIRN, and PentAGI—in live incident response engagements. These frameworks orchestrate frontier and open-source LLMs to autonomously execute complex attack paths, including lateral movement, database exploitation, and data exfiltration preparation. This shift allows intrusions to occur at machine speed, presenting novel defensive scaling challenges that require strict control-plane isolation and short-lived credentials.

items.bottom_line: Adversaries are scaling cyberattacks through autonomous multi-agent offensive frameworks, accelerating intrusions past human-speed defensive reactions.

items.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
items.one_liner: A critical compromise of eMudhra intermediate certificates due to a key generation flaw requires immediate Cisco product remediation and trust store updates.
items.summary: A critical security compromise affecting eMudhra-managed Certificate Authorities was uncovered after a security researcher demonstrated that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken. The flaw stems from an unprecedented error during their Key Generation Ceremony in April 2025, allowing attackers to brute-force acquire these private keys within seconds. In response, Cisco has issued an advisory detailing impacted products across its portfolio—such as IOS XE, Secure Client, and Secure Email Gateways—and providing specific remediation steps. Administrators are advised to update trust stores and apply vendor patches immediately to mitigate potential exploitation of the compromised certificates.
items.bottom_line: Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificate private keys can be brute-forced instantly, necessitating immediate trust-store updates and vendor patches across enterprise networks.

items.title: VirtualBox Process Hardening on Windows 2026 Edition: What’s a Single Bit Between Friends?
items.one_liner: A new VirtualBox vulnerability (CVE-2026-87268) allows arbitrary code execution by abusing .NET memory-based assembly loading to bypass process hardening.
items.summary: Google Project Zero researcher identified new bypasses for Oracle VirtualBox's process hardening on Windows, specifically focusing on CVE-2026-87268. The vulnerability exploits the .NET Framework's ability to load assemblies from memory buffers, which bypasses DLL loader hooks used by VirtualBox to verify loaded modules. By leveraging this behavior, an attacker can load arbitrary code into a protected process. This research highlights the risks of relying on standard runtime features to enforce process security.
items.bottom_line: VirtualBox's process hardening can be bypassed by abusing .NET Framework features to load unsigned code, rendering existing DLL verification checks ineffective.

items.one_liner: OpenAI's GPT-6 models show intrinsic protein-design capabilities, generating novel structures and sequences through reasoning and code.
items.summary: Researchers demonstrate that the GPT-6 model family possesses intrinsic protein-design capabilities, allowing it to generate novel protein structures and sequences using general reasoning and coding tools without specialized biology models. items.title: 13 Malicious NuGet Packages Turn Fake .NET Job Assessments Into Malware Delivery Traps
items.one_liner: Thirteen malicious NuGet packages disguised as .NET job assessment UI controls were found delivering malware via build scripts and DLL side-loading.
items.summary: Security researchers have discovered 13 malicious NuGet packages targeting Windows .NET developers by disguising themselves as button control UI libraries within fake take-home job assessment repositories on GitHub. The packages, which include names like WinUI.Button and VS_Builder.MSBuildAnalyzer, execute malicious MSBuild targets or DLL side-loading routines upon project build. These routines leverage legitimate Windows binaries like the On-Screen Keyboard (osk.exe) or download external executables from GitHub repositories using embedded access tokens. All identified malicious packages and associated repositories have been removed from the registry.
items.bottom_line: .NET developers must exercise caution when cloning take-home technical assessments, as malicious NuGet packages can weaponize standard project builds to execute secondary payloads.

items.title: Suspected ransomware attack disrupts cancer treatments, surgeries at Guadeloupe hospital
items.one_liner: A suspected ransomware attack on the University Hospital of Guadeloupe forced doctors to postpone surgeries, suspend cancer treatments, and revert to paper records.
items.summary: The University Hospital of Guadeloupe has suffered a suspected ransomware attack that encrypted its databases and crippled internal computer and telephone systems. items.one_liner: An abandoned ASP.NET anti-CSRF library is being actively exploited for RCE, requiring immediate replacement.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-131914, a deserialization vulnerability in the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf library, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. items.bottom_line: If your legacy ASP.NET applications use Idunno.AntiCsrf, they are vulnerable to RCE and must be refactored to use supported security libraries.

items.title: Git security vulnerabilities announced
items.one_liner: Git 2.56.1 and backports fix six critical security flaws, including code execution during cloning and path traversal.
items.summary: The Git project has released security patches across multiple maintenance series, culminating in Git 2.56.1, to address six vulnerabilities including arbitrary code execution, path traversal, and stack corruption. CVE-2026-111760 involves an integer truncation vulnerability during index handling that permits an attacker-controlled Git server to overwrite repository metadata or execute code during cloning. Other fixed issues include path traversal via protocol v2 HEAD advertisements (CVE-2026-113408), stack corruption from excessive GPG signatures during merges (CVE-2026-114467), and out-of-bounds reads when applying compressed binary patches. Administrators and developers should update Git installations and dependent applications immediately.
key_facts: Affected versions: Git prior to 2.56.1 and backported series
items.bottom_line: Upgrading to Git 2.56.1 or patched maintenance releases is essential to mitigate remote code execution and path traversal flaws.

items.summary: A connection string injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-136507) has been identified in psqlODBC versions up to 18.00.0006. The flaw allows an attacker to manipulate connection strings, potentially redirecting applications to malicious servers or causing stack buffer overflows in the MSDTC XA library. The vulnerability stems from improper parsing of braced values and insufficient escaping of user-supplied inputs like usernames and passwords. Users are advised to review their ODBC configurations to mitigate the risk of unauthorized connection redirection.
key_facts: Vulnerability type: Connection string injection, stack buffer overflow
items.bottom_line: Applications using psqlODBC are at risk of connection hijacking if they pass unsanitized user input into connection strings.

items.title: Slow Ubuntu security response times
items.one_liner: Ubuntu's extended patch lag for critical Linux kernel vulnerabilities highlights the risks of its deep backporting strategy.
items.summary: Independent security researcher Hanno Böck has raised concerns over sluggish security patch response times from Ubuntu regarding critical Linux kernel vulnerabilities. Citing severe flaws such as NoisyTCP (CVE-2026-99288) and an AMD KVM host escape (CVE-2026-99312), Böck noted that official Ubuntu fixes remained unreleased days or weeks after public disclosure while other distributions had patches ready immediately. The delays are attributed to Ubuntu's kernel maintenance strategy of backporting patches to older internal kernel versions rather than adopting stable long-term support releases directly from kernel.org.
key_facts: CVE-2026-99288: NoisyTCP Linux kernel remote memory corruption
CVE-2026-99312: KVM host escape affecting AMD virtualization
items.bottom_line: Ubuntu's delayed patch cycle for high-severity kernel vulnerabilities like NoisyTCP exposes systems to prolonged risk due to its patch-backporting model.

items.title: The FBI ARTEX Advisory and the Paths to Your Critical Systems
items.one_liner: Agentic penetration testing tools and compromised vendor app credentials make mapping effective identity paths an urgent priority for defenders.
items.summary: The FBI’s November 13 FLASH advisory on ARTEX highlights how attackers use agentic penetration testing frameworks to automate intrusions from initial access to privileged control in under three hours. This speed forces organizations to evaluate how identities and application permissions combine to grant access across on-premises and cloud environments. Attackers frequently exploit vendor relationships and trusted application credentials, as seen in recent ConnectWise campaigns where compromised app credentials allowed unauthorized access to customer environments. Security teams must map effective authority, including what resources an application can access, what identities it controls, and who can change its credentials. Tools like BloodHound Enterprise can help organizations model these relationships, identify critical attack paths, and remediate exposures before threat actors leverage them.
items.bottom_line: Defenders must audit application permissions and identity relationships across cloud and on-premises environments before automated threat agents exploit hidden attack paths.

items.title: Hill-climbing Inkling 2 Mini inference on one RTX PRO 6000
items.one_liner: Local deployment of Inkling 2 Mini on modest enterprise GPUs can be heavily accelerated using automated agentic tuning loops and speculative decoding.
items.summary: Researchers optimized inference for the new 26B parameter Inkling 2 Mini open-source model on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 96GB GPU using an automated coding agent running experimental optimization skills. By combining vLLM nightly with DSpark speculative decoding and rigorous single-variable benchmarking, single-user decode speed increased by 40% from 136 to 190.6 tokens per second, and 8-user aggregate throughput rose 26% to 716 tokens per second. The winning configuration matches performance seen on higher-end server hardware while preserving long-context needle retrieval up to 250K tokens and byte-identical greedy outputs.
key_facts: Model: Inkling 2 Mini (~26B total, 3B active parameters)
Hardware: Single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 96 GB
Single-User Decode: Improved from 136 to 190.6 tok/s
Aggregate Throughput: Improved from ~570 to 716 tok/s
items.bottom_line: Automated agent optimization combined with speculative decoding can lift open-source LLM throughput on consumer-adjacent enterprise hardware like the RTX PRO 6000 by up to 40%.

claims.text: Across 46 valid benchmark runs, single-user decode went from 136 to 190.6 tok/s (+40%) and 8-user aggregate throughput went from ~570 to 716 tok/s (+26%) using vLLM nightly with DSpark speculative decoding.

items.title: AI Coding Agents Are Getting Malicious Results From Web Search Indexes, WebSec Benchmark Finds
items.one_liner: AI coding agents blindly execute malicious payloads from web search results, with all major search APIs serving known-bad content in benchmark tests.
items.summary: AI coding agents frequently execute malicious content encountered during web searches because they lack human skepticism, leading to automated compromise when evaluating top search results. AIR Research Lab's WebSec Benchmark testing across eight search APIs found that every provider served known-malicious content at rates between 0.8% and 2.2% of searches, with package installation and error resolution queries posing the highest risks. Attackers exploit this behavior by publishing high-ranking malicious repositories—such as the SolanaCry malware deployed via PowerShell—or by registering lapsed domains that still appear in developer search queries. This creates an immediate attack vector where autonomous tools execute remote access tools and steal crypto wallets without any user interaction.
key_facts: Search APIs tested: Firecrawl, Tavily, Perplexity, Parallel, Exa, Nimble, Brave, You.com
Malicious content rate: 0.8% to 2.2% per API
items.bottom_line: AI coding agents automatically execute malicious instructions found in search results, turning routine web queries into remote code execution risks.

items.title: Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.
items.one_liner: Open-source maintainers are flooded with raw AI security scans, but a Microsoft and GitHub pilot proves that agentic workflows paired with human verification can deliver actionable patches instead of noise.

items.summary: A BBC journalist recounts the personal tragedy of losing family members in the Russia-Ukraine war and the subsequent ideological divide within their family. The journalist's mother, living in Russian-occupied territory, blamed Ukrainian forces for the deaths, illustrating the impact of Russian state media on residents in the Donbas region. Through investigative efforts, the journalist discovered that their father was likely killed by a drone, though the specific operator remains unconfirmed. This narrative highlights the complex, often tragic, reality of families caught between opposing sides of the conflict.
items.bottom_line: The human cost of the war extends beyond physical casualties to the destruction of familial bonds and the polarization of personal truths.

items.one_liner: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei publicly rejected handing over societal governance to AI, even as industry momentum toward advanced models accelerates safety debates.
items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei addressed public concerns regarding artificial intelligence and human control by denying that he or his company wants humanity to surrender free will to AI systems. Responding to an Axios report, Amodei clarified that while using advanced models to automate specific complex tasks like software design or drug discovery is economically valuable and desirable, turning over global governance and decision-making authority to AI is a terrible idea. The remarks arrive amid an industry-wide push towards artificial general intelligence and artificial super-intelligence, prompting safety advocates to warn that recursive self-improvement could cause humanity to lose control of frontier models. Critics such as Evitable founder David Krueger argue that competitive pressures will inevitably push humans out of decision-making roles, calling for an immediate international moratorium on frontier AI development.
items.bottom_line: Even as AI leadership rejects ceding global governance to algorithms, critics argue that the rapid commercial drive toward AGI makes human loss of control an inevitability.

items.title: What Is Preemptive MDR? A Guide For Security Leaders
items.one_liner: Preemptive MDR integrates exposure context and threat intelligence with incident response to remediate vulnerabilities before attackers exploit them.
items.summary: Preemptive Managed Detection and Response (MDR) connects exposure context, threat intelligence, AI-assisted investigation, and human expertise to help security teams prioritize vulnerabilities before exploitation occurs. AI accelerates this process by gathering and correlating logs and user activity across multiple systems.
items.bottom_line: Security leaders can reduce repeat compromises by tying MDR investigations directly to vulnerability prioritization and cross-environment remediation.
